advances:
Gives an exact rational compatible counterexample to the joint
support-width inequality registered in `tail-middle-cap-width-coupling`.
The strict deficit is \(41/240\), and every canonical-tail hypothesis,
including the exact residual chamber, \(D_0>m\), and the strict \(q\)-tail,
is verified directly.  The two true optimized endpoint sums are \(0\) and
\(m\); consequently \(I_\ell=\varnothing\).  Thus the candidate refutes the
registered joint \(\Psi\)-inequality but is not a counterexample to
`canonical-tail-exclusion` or to the locked theorem.

The same instance also isolates why the proposed row-triangle reduction
cannot repair this failure.  The support-minimal row-aligned triangle
containing the fixed midpoint body has area
\(441294049/320000\), whereas the residual upper bound is \(9/8\).
author: r099_tail_triangle_reduction
proof:
The sets in (3)-(5) are rational rectangles with positive side lengths.
The functions in (2) are nonconstant, their linear parts
\[
(-1,0),\qquad(0,-1),\qquad(1,1)
\]
are pairwise nonparallel, and their sum is \(-1\).  Hence all affine
requirements in `canonical-tail-exclusion` hold.

The midpoint of the two \(x\)-intervals in the Minkowski sense is
\[
\frac12\left(
\left[-\frac{11}{800},-\frac3{800}\right]
+
\left[-\frac{17}{800},\frac3{800}\right]
\right)
=\left[-\frac7{400},0\right].
\]
Similarly,
\[
\frac12\left(
\left[-\frac{165}{4},\frac{235}{4}\right]
+
\left[\frac{25}{4},\frac{45}{4}\right]
\right)
=\left[-\frac{35}{2},35\right].
\]
This proves (6), so the three slices are compatible, in fact with equality
in midpoint containment.

The side lengths of \(A_0\) are \(1/100\) and \(100\), while those of
\(A_2\) are \(1/40\) and \(5\).  The side lengths of \(K\) are \(7/400\)
and \(105/2\).  Therefore
\[
|A_0|=1,\qquad
|A_2|=\frac18,\qquad
|K|=\frac7{400}\cdot\frac{105}{2}
=\frac{147}{160},
\]
which gives (7).  Here
\[
\frac mM=\frac18<\frac9{25}.
\]
In this branch, accepted fact `15bb2c1680a0254e` gives the exact residual
interval
\[
1-\frac18<\frac kM<1+\frac18.
\]
It holds strictly because
\[
\frac78=\frac{140}{160}
<
\frac{147}{160}
<
\frac{180}{160}=\frac98.
\tag{18}
\]
Thus every residual area hypothesis is satisfied.  Direct substitution
also gives
\[
3t-k-m
=\frac{109}{80}-\frac{147}{160}-\frac18
=\frac{51}{160}
>\frac18,
\]
proving (8).

Since \(K\subseteq\{x\le0\}\), its \(i\)-cap is the null edge \(x=0\),
so \(c_i=0\).  Its \(\ell\)-cap is a rectangle of width \(7/400\) and
height \(35\), which gives \(c_\ell=49/80\).  For every
\(x\in[-7/400,0]\), the line \(x+y=1\) crosses the interior of the
vertical interval of \(K\).  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
c_q
&=\int_{-7/400}^{0}
\left(1-x+\frac{35}{2}\right)\,dx\\
&=\int_{-7/400}^{0}
\left(\frac{37}{2}-x\right)\,dx
=\frac{103649}{320000}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{19}
\]
The exact tail slack is
\[
t-m-c_q
=\frac{109}{240}-\frac18-\frac{103649}{320000}
=\frac{5053}{960000}>0,
\tag{20}
\]
which proves (9)-(10).  In particular, for all sufficiently negative
shifts \(a\), the \(A_0\) \(q\)-cap is empty and the \(A_2\) \(q\)-cap is
full, so \(\mu_q(a)=c_q+m<t\), as required by the canonical tail branch.

We next compute the support-width profiles.  In the \(i\)-direction,
\[
\beta_{0i}=-\frac3{800},\qquad
\beta_{2i}=\frac3{800},\qquad
w_{0i}=\frac1{100},\qquad
w_{2i}=\frac1{40}.
\]
It follows that
\[
R_i=0,\qquad
\sigma_i
=\left(\frac1{100}\right)^2
+\frac{(1/40)^2}{1/8}
=\frac{51}{10000},
\]
and therefore \(\Psi_i(R_i)=0\).

In the \(\ell\)-direction,
\[
\beta_{0\ell}=\frac{235}{4},\qquad
\beta_{2\ell}=\frac{45}{4},\qquad
w_{0\ell}=100,\qquad
w_{2\ell}=5.
\]
Thus
\[
R_\ell=70,\qquad
\sigma_\ell
=100^2+\frac{5^2}{1/8}
=10200.
\]
Since
\[
\frac{R_\ell^2}{\sigma_\ell}
=\frac{4900}{10200}
=\frac{49}{102}
>\frac18=m,
\]
the profile is on its plateau and
\(\Psi_\ell(R_\ell)=m=1/8\).  Finally,
\[
2t-c_i-c_\ell
=\frac{109}{120}-\frac{49}{80}
=\frac{71}{240},
\]
and
\[
\frac{71}{240}-\frac18
=\frac{41}{240}>0.
\]
This proves the strict failure (12), including its exact deficit.

It remains to compute the true endpoint optima in (14).  In the \(i\)-row,
take \(a=3/800\).  Then
\[
A_0\cap\{f_i\le a\}
=A_0\cap\left\{x\ge-\frac3{800}\right\}
\]
and
\[
A_2\cap\{f_i\le-a\}
=A_2\cap\left\{x\ge\frac3{800}\right\}
\]
are null support edges.  Hence \(\Phi_i(3/800)=0\), and nonnegativity gives
\(\inf_a\Phi_i(a)=0\).

For the \(\ell\)-row,
\[
A_0\cap\{f_\ell\le a\}=A_0\cap\{y\ge-a\},
\qquad
A_2\cap\{f_\ell\le-a\}=A_2\cap\{y\ge a\}.
\tag{21}
\]
If \(a\le25/4\), the second cap in (21) is all of \(A_2\), so
\(\Phi_\ell(a)\ge m\).  If \(a>25/4\), then the first cap contains
\[
A_0\cap\left\{y\ge-\frac{25}{4}\right\},
\]
whose area is
\[
\frac1{100}
\left(\frac{235}{4}+\frac{25}{4}\right)
=\frac{13}{20}>m.
\]
Thus \(\Phi_\ell(a)\ge m\) for every real \(a\).  At
\(a=-235/4\), the first cap in (21) is the null top edge of \(A_0\),
while the second is all of \(A_2\).  Equality is attained, proving
\(\inf_a\Phi_\ell(a)=m\).  Equations (9), (13), and (14) now give (15).
This exact true-profile calculation shows why the counterexample to the
\(\Psi\)-inequality does not propagate to canonical tail exclusion:
\(I_\ell\) is empty.

For completeness, consider the row-triangle obstruction.  If the triangle
in (16) contains \(K\), then its three facet bounds must dominate the
corresponding supports of \(K\):
\[
a\ge\frac7{400},\qquad
b\ge\frac{35}{2},\qquad
c\ge35.
\tag{22}
\]
In the standard \((x,y)\)-coordinates, its area is
\[
|\widetilde K(a,b,c)|=\frac{(a+b+c)^2}{2}.
\tag{23}
\]
The support-minimal choice in (22) has
\[
a+b+c
=\frac7{400}+\frac{35}{2}+35
=\frac{21007}{400}.
\]
Equations (22)-(23) therefore yield
\[
|\widetilde K(a,b,c)|
\ge
\frac12\left(\frac{21007}{400}\right)^2
=\frac{441294049}{320000}.
\tag{24}
\]
For the unchanged endpoint areas \(M=1,m=1/8\), the strict residual upper
bound from `15bb2c1680a0254e` is
\[
\widetilde k<M+m=\frac98.
\]
Since the right side of (24) is larger than \(9/8\), no row-aligned
triangle containing the fixed midpoint body can satisfy the residual
domain.  This obstruction concerns row-support-hull area, not cap
monotonicity.

The candidate proves only that the registered joint \(\Psi\)-inequality is
too strong and that the stated unrestricted triangle reduction is
unavailable.  Because \(I_\ell=\varnothing\), it supplies no counterexample
to `canonical-tail-exclusion`, the original three-slice depth statement, or
the locked theorem.
statement:
Work in the standard \((x,y)\)-plane and put
\[
g_i=x,\qquad g_\ell=y,\qquad g_q=1-x-y,
\tag{1}
\]
or equivalently
\[
f_i=-x,\qquad f_\ell=-y,\qquad f_q=x+y-1.
\tag{2}
\]
Define
\[
A_0=
\left[-\frac{11}{800},-\frac3{800}\right]
\times
\left[-\frac{165}{4},\frac{235}{4}\right],
\tag{3}
\]
\[
A_2=
\left[-\frac{17}{800},\frac3{800}\right]
\times
\left[\frac{25}{4},\frac{45}{4}\right],
\tag{4}
\]
and
\[
K=
\left[-\frac7{400},0\right]
\times
\left[-\frac{35}{2},35\right].
\tag{5}
\]
Then \(A_0,A_2,K\) are nonempty two-dimensional rational convex
polytopes satisfying
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}=K.
\tag{6}
\]
Writing
\[
M=|A_0|,\qquad m=|A_2|,\qquad k=|K|,
\qquad t=\frac{2(M+m+k)}9,
\]
one has
\[
M=1,\qquad m=\frac18,\qquad k=\frac{147}{160},
\qquad t=\frac{109}{240}.
\tag{7}
\]
The area triple lies in the exact strict residual chamber of accepted fact
`15bb2c1680a0254e`, and
\[
D_0=3t-k-m=\frac{51}{160}>m.
\tag{8}
\]

For \(j\in\{i,\ell,q\}\), let
\[
c_j=|K\cap\{g_j\ge0\}|.
\]
Then
\[
c_i=0,\qquad
c_\ell=\frac{49}{80},\qquad
c_q=\frac{103649}{320000},
\tag{9}
\]
and the \(q\)-tail is strict:
\[
c_q+m<t.
\tag{10}
\]

For \(r\in\{0,2\}\) and \(j\in\{i,\ell\}\), define
\[
\alpha_{rj}=\min_{A_r}g_j,\qquad
\beta_{rj}=\max_{A_r}g_j,\qquad
w_{rj}=\beta_{rj}-\alpha_{rj},
\]
\[
R_j=\beta_{0j}+\beta_{2j},\qquad
\sigma_j=\frac{w_{0j}^2}{M}+\frac{w_{2j}^2}{m},
\]
and
\[
\Psi_j(R)=
\begin{cases}
0,&R\le0,\\
\min\{R^2/\sigma_j,m\},&R>0.
\end{cases}
\]
For the rectangles (3)-(4),
\[
\Psi_i(R_i)=0,\qquad
\Psi_\ell(R_\ell)=\frac18.
\tag{11}
\]
Nevertheless,
\[
\Psi_i(R_i)+\Psi_\ell(R_\ell)
=\frac18
<
\frac{71}{240}
=2t-c_i-c_\ell.
\tag{12}
\]
Thus (3)-(5) are an exact counterexample to the displayed conclusion of
`tail-middle-cap-width-coupling`.

For the true endpoint contribution
\[
\Phi_j(a)=
|A_0\cap\{f_j\le a\}|
+|A_2\cap\{f_j\le-a\}|,
\tag{13}
\]
the exact optimized values are
\[
\inf_{a\in\mathbb R}\Phi_i(a)=0,
\qquad
\inf_{a\in\mathbb R}\Phi_\ell(a)=\frac18=m.
\tag{14}
\]
Consequently
\[
\inf_a\mu_\ell(a)
=c_\ell+\inf_a\Phi_\ell(a)
=\frac{59}{80}
>t,
\tag{15}
\]
and hence \(I_\ell=\varnothing\).  In particular, this candidate does not
refute canonical tail exclusion.

Finally, every row-aligned triangle
\[
\widetilde K(a,b,c)
=\{(x,y):x\ge-a,\ y\ge-b,\ x+y\le c\}
\tag{16}
\]
that contains the same midpoint body \((A_0+A_2)/2=K\) has
\[
|\widetilde K(a,b,c)|
\ge\frac{441294049}{320000}
>\frac98=M+m.
\tag{17}
\]
Thus no such triangle remains in the strict residual area chamber.
